direction.premise: An industrial precision range where the targets are physical enamel-and-steel mechanisms, not abstract dots or simulated enemies.
direction.composition: The horizontal training world fills the main viewport; a narrow equipment rail chooses drills on the left, while the live range remains unobstructed and its ledger sits outside the playfield.
direction.shapeLanguage: Target plates use concentric hard circles, four visible rivets and short rail-mounted silhouettes; the interface uses square cuts, thin measurement rules and restrained mechanical marks.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: The arena is charcoal-painted steel with brushed rails, warm ceramic faces and small brass fasteners; the surrounding controls are dry parchment and dark green enamel.
direction.paletteLogic: Deep green-black recedes behind the reticle, parchment carries all readable text, rust marks active targets and hit response, and brass is reserved for the central scoring rings.
direction.typography: Georgia carries the workshop's measured editorial voice, while compact monospace labels identify drill codes, times and scores without competing with the live target.
direction.signature: A hit spins the target plate off its axis and releases a short spray of enamel and steel fragments; the impact ring remains briefly where the target was.
direction.distinction: Unlike Press's file ledger, Pereves's suspended balance sculpture, Echolot's sonar instrument, Emergent Kingdoms's map and Folkarium's notation spread, Flickyard is a mouse-first open range with moving physical targets.

architecture.primaryVerb: Move the mouse to acquire a moving plate, make one deliberate correction and click when the reticle settles inside its center.
architecture.physicalFeedback: A successful shot rotates the plate away from its rail, sheds a few hard fragments and produces a short ceramic-metal impact; a miss gives a quieter felt-backed knock.
architecture.spatialRationale: The range must preserve broad horizontal mouse travel and a stable 16:9 target field; the left rail stays outside the canvas, while mobile collapses it into a compact drill selector above the scene.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Press is a split file-processing workspace with a permanent operation rail and a measurable file ledger; Flickyard gives most of the screen to one continuous target field.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Press selects files and runs discrete conversion jobs; Flickyard continuously samples mouse movement and resolves each shot against a live moving target.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Pereves presents a light gallery wall and a suspended sculpture with a separate object table; Flickyard is a wide dark range with targets mounted on horizontal steel tracks.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Pereves places physical weights to solve static torque; Flickyard moves a reticle directly and times clicks against targets with changing trajectories.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Echolot centers a circular sonar instrument with its own perimeter controls; Flickyard keeps an open rectangular range and places the drill selector outside the playable area.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Echolot spends oxygen to scan and reveal hidden geography; Flickyard uses continuous pointer control, timed shots and on-target tracking time.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Emergent Kingdoms is a cartographic study with a persistent chronology and side journal; Flickyard has no map, timeline or data layers, only a live target range.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Emergent Kingdoms advances autonomous yearly simulation and branches history; Flickyard responds to millisecond mouse input and immediate target contact.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Folkarium is a landscape manuscript spread with instrument columns and an editable staff; Flickyard is a full-bleed arena with a small external drill rail.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Folkarium edits pitches and auditions musical parts; Flickyard tracks mouse coordinates, target timing and hit registration.

production.renderer: Canvas 2D owns the high-frequency range, target motion and impact particles; semantic DOM and CSS keep settings, results and drill navigation sharp and accessible.
production.focalAsset: The focal object is an original concentric enamel target plate with four rivets, a dark steel backing and a rust-red center, drawn from vector geometry in Canvas.

motion.character: Target motion is mechanical and legible: rails carry steady travel, direction changes have a brief angular correction, and impact rotation carries inertia rather than a soft UI bounce.
motion.action: The player moves a reticle with the mouse, fires once with the left button or holds it during the tracking drill, and immediately sees the result at the contact point.
motion.anticipation: The active switching target gains a restrained rust outline and a small outer pulse before the player transfers aim; no full-screen warning or flashing effect is used.
motion.response: On the first hit frame the plate turns, the score increments, a small ring expands from the impact and a few fragments inherit the target's outward velocity.
motion.followThrough: Fragments fall and lose speed while the target is replaced; the score remains stable in the HUD and the next target appears without a scene transition.
motion.interruption: A new shot is processed immediately, pause cancels the animation loop and releases pointer capture, and Escape never queues movement or delayed firing.
motion.reducedMotion: The target position and hit result remain immediate and readable; reduced motion removes fragment spray, pulsing rings and nonessential settling transitions.

evidence.expectedChange: The menu overlay disappears, the live HUD appears and a target becomes available for direct mouse aiming in the range.
